diagnostic_evidence.quote: the maximum of $1$ and the implicit constants from \eqref{eq:Rekalpha4H1} and \eqref{eq:Rekalpha4L2}

issues.failure_explanation: The last inequality absorbs the term cT_1^{1/2}Err_m into (1/2)Err_m, which requires cT_1^{1/2} <= 1/2. However, c is defined as the maximum of 1 and the implicit constants, and T_1 := min{T, b_0, c^{-2}} only yields cT_1^{1/2} <= c*c^{-1} = 1. In the admissible case T_1 = c^{-2} the coefficient equals 1, so the absorption yields nothing and the key recursion (4.24) is not established as written.

failure_location.quote: \mathrm{Err}_m \le c\|E_{N_m}\|_{H^1 \times L^2} + c\tau^\frac12 + cT_1^{\frac12}\mathrm{Err}_m \le c\mathrm{Err}_{m-1} + c\tau^\frac12 + \frac12 \mathrm{Err}_m.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Shrink the prescribed time step of the iteration by a forced constant factor, e.g., redefine T_1 := min{T, b_0, (2c)^{-2}} (equivalently impose cT_1^{1/2} <= 1/2) in DefT1New. All other steps of the argument are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The recursive estimate ErrRekursionNew, and with it the energy-norm and L^2 x H^{-1} global error bounds for alpha=4 in Theorem ThmStrang, are unjustified as written. The alpha=4 part of Theorem ThmStrangFully is affected as well, since its proof is closed "as in the semi-discrete case", i.e., by the same iteration with the same choice of T_1.
issues.title: Smallness condition on T_1 does not justify the absorption step in the alpha=4 error iteration
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single forced change of one constant in a standard smallness condition; the iterative argument, the convergence rates tau^{1/2} and tau^{3/2}, and every stated guarantee survive verbatim, with no new lemma, construction, reoptimization, or loss of scope.
